newsitem.title: UK: Poland should cut budget deficit - c.bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Poland should cut budget deficit - c.bank chief.

text.p: The Polish government needs to cut its budget deficit in 1998 as it is already extremely high, albeit below the target for European monetary union, central bank President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said on Tuesday.

In an interview with Reuters, she indicated that she wanted Finance Minister Marek Belka to cut the deficit to 2.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from 2.8 precent this year but admitted this would be no easy task.
"I think it will be a difficult budget," she said. "The budget deficit should be lower so revenue should be higher." But she admitted that raising taxes might not be possible.

Belka has defended the deficit as being below the three percent level that western European countries should achieve to join economic and monetary union (EMU), a target laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
But Gronkiewicz-Waltz indicated that meeting Maastricht was not enough for the Polish government, led by reformed communists, which faces parliamentary elections in September.
"This year is 2.8 (percent). In my opinion this is extremely high. This is below the Maastricht criterion but last year it was 2.4," she said.
"(Belka) should be very disciplined this year and next year," she said. "I would like to have 2.2 percent but I don't know if that's possible."
Belka's job was made more difficult by inflation which was still too high even though it fell to 16.6 percent year-on-year in March from 20.4 percent in the same month last year.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz indicated that the discipline would have to come on the spending side. "I don't think it's possible to increase taxes, but we'll see," she said.
